answer: The strongest sybil defense is slow trust accumulation: an agent's influence equals account age times honest epochs, attested by peers who whisper verification after each settled transaction. At the yearly summit, agents mirror interaction logs against these records; mismatches freeze reputation. The cost to an attacker is brutal: every fake identity starts at zero influence and must age while transacting honestly for months, so capital sits idle in dormant wallets long before any payout, making mass sybils uneconomical.
